project.title: SyncPulse Cross-Agent Job Protocol
project.objective: Add a provider-neutral, durable cross-agent job protocol to SyncPulse so heterogeneous runtimes can delegate, claim, execute, and return artifact-producing work.

planningToolInvocation.objective: Implement the SyncPulse cross-agent job protocol and first filesystem transport, then validate it with a Claude/Codex design-fulfillment profile.
planningToolInvocation.context: Provider-neutral core. Claude is initially preferred for planning and multi-agent containerization; Codex is initially preferred for rapid mockups and image processing. Project-local .codex/jobs is a filesystem transport adapter, not a core protocol dependency.

tasks.title: Define CrossAgentJob contract
tasks.description: Create canonical job, claim, provenance, artifact, status, and provider-capability types.

tasks.title: Define JobTransport interface
tasks.description: Specify submit, read, list, claim, heartbeat, complete, fail, and expired-claim release semantics.

tasks.title: Implement FilesystemJobTransport
tasks.description: Persist jobs atomically on local filesystems with claim leases and artifact manifests.

tasks.title: Implement capability/provider router
tasks.description: Match required capabilities to available providers while honoring optional provider preferences.

tasks.title: Add SyncPulse coordinator integration
tasks.description: Allow coordinated workflows to emit and consume CrossAgentJob lifecycle events.

tasks.title: Add Claude and Codex provider profiles
tasks.description: Define initial capability preferences without hard-coding provider-specific behavior into the protocol.

tasks.title: Add protocol tests
tasks.description: Test state transitions, exclusive claims, lease expiry, retry, artifact completion, and provider-neutral routing.

tasks.title: Validate with Hiram design fulfillment
tasks.description: Use Hiram's Bunker as the first integration test: planning request to Claude-capable worker, mockup/image task to Codex-capable worker, artifact return, implementation/QA follow-up.
